Kuvitus: ultraäänitutkimus. Potilas maka: Illustration: an ultrasound examination. A patient lies on their back on an examination table. A nurse stands beside the table and presses an ultrasound probe on the patient's abdomen, where the skin has a translucent gel. Curved wavefronts spread from the probe into the body. The cable of the probe runs to the ultrasound machine, whose screen shows a grey fan-shaped image.
Kaavakuva, ei mittakaavassa: ultraäänian: Schematic figure, not to scale: an ultrasound probe is on the skin, with a thin layer of gel between the probe and the skin. Under the skin, one below the other, are a layer of fat, muscle and bone. A blue arrow shows the pulse travelling down from the probe and its speed. From the boundary of fat and muscle and from the boundary of muscle and bone an echo returns upwards, shown by thinner blue arrows. On the left a dimension line shows the depth d from the surface of the skin to the boundary of muscle and bone.
Kaavakuva: kaksi ultraäänianturia vierek: Schematic figure: two ultrasound probes side by side send a pulse into the same tissue. On the left the frequency is 3 MHz and the wavelength about 0.5 mm, on the right the frequency is 12 MHz and the wavelength about 0.13 mm. The spacing of the wavefronts has been enlarged, but their ratio of four to one is correct. The wavefronts of the left wave fade slowly and reach a depth of about 17 cm, the wavefronts of the right wave fade already at a depth of about 4 cm. The depth scale on the left is in centimetres.
Kaavakuva Maan poikkileikkauksesta, kerr: Schematic figure of a cross-section of the Earth, the radii of the layers to scale, the curvature of the rays only indicative: outermost the mantle, inside it the liquid outer core and in the middle the solid inner core. The earthquake is at the top on the surface. Three rays of the P wave set out to the right as continuous lines, and one P wave travels through the core to the opposite side of the Earth. Three rays of the S wave set out to the left as dashed lines; an S wave that meets the outer core stops at its surface. On the surface of the Earth opposite the earthquake is the shadow zone of S waves, which begins at an angular distance of about 103 degrees from the earthquake.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: P- ja S-aallon ku: Graph to scale: the travel time t of the P wave and the S wave in seconds as a function of the distance d in kilometres from zero to 300 kilometres, when the speed of the P wave is 6.0 km/s and that of the S wave 3.5 km/s. Each is a straight line rising from the origin; the line of the S wave is steeper. At a distance of 105 km the travel time of the P wave is 17.5 s and that of the S wave 30 s, and their difference, 12.5 s, is marked with a vertical segment.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: matalan veden aal: Graph to scale: the speed v of a shallow-water wave in metres per second as a function of the depth h of the water in metres from zero to 5000 metres, when v is the square root of g times h. The curve rises steeply in shallow water and flattens out deeper. At a depth of 4000 m the speed is about 198 m/s and at a depth of 1000 m about 99 m/s; both points are marked.
Kuvaaja, keksitty esimerkkiaineisto: ult: Graph, invented example data: an A-scan of a thigh from an ultrasound machine. On the horizontal axis the time t in microseconds from the sending of the pulse from zero to 110 microseconds, grid lines at intervals of five microseconds and values at intervals of 20 microseconds. On the vertical axis the strength of the echo as a relative value. At the moment zero there is a tall transmitted pulse. The echoes: A at the moment 20 µs, low; B at the moment 50 µs, lower; C at the moment 90 µs, tall. After echo C the curve stays at zero.
Kuvaaja, mallin laskemia arvoja: kolmen: Graph, values calculated by a model: the seismograms of three seismograph stations one below the other, the time t in seconds from the earthquake from zero to 80 seconds, grid lines at intervals of two seconds and values at intervals of ten seconds. The top station is 84 km, the middle one 168 km and the bottom one 252 km from the earthquake. In each curve a small oscillation, the P wave, starts first and later a larger one, the S wave; the start moments are marked with the letters P and S. In the top one P starts at 14 s and S at 24 s, in the middle one P at 28 s and S at 48 s, in the bottom one P at 42 s and S at 72 s. Surface waves have been left out.
Kuvaaja, keksitty esimerkkiaineisto: yhd: Graph, invented example data: the seismogram of one seismograph station, the time t in seconds from the start of the recording from zero to 50 seconds, grid lines at intervals of two seconds and values at intervals of ten seconds. A small oscillation, the P wave, starts at 12 s and a larger one, the S wave, at 30 s; the start moments are marked with the letters P and S.
